review_method: Visual review of timestamped overview frames, transition samples and three 0.25-second sequences. Not a frame-by-frame review of every original frame; no source code from the video was available.
timestamps_reference: The uploaded recording, not the YouTube player time shown inside it.

observations.evidence: Night combat with firearms. Overlay reads avgPing:129, deltaPing:12, delay:25.
Two nearby players with spears. Overlay reads avgPing:117, deltaPing:-11, delay:41, lead:117.
Overlay reads avgPing:115 and lead:115. Repeated samples in 24.50–28.00 also show lead matching avgPing.

Visible targeting line continues to the player labelled [DRUGS] #12 while the two players move; spear-like projectiles and hit feedback are visible. This does not establish the exact selection algorithm or count confirmed hits.
Inventory hover explicitly reads Wood Spear, Don’t forget to pick it up, Damage:80.
Several players and a moving targeting line are visible. The nearest-target versus fixed-lock versus manual selection rule cannot be established from these frames.

interpretations.claim: Aim prediction probably accounts for network delay.
interpretations.basis: avgPing and lead are displayed and repeatedly equal in one segment; displayed values alone do not prove how they enter the calculation.

interpretations.claim: The observed behavior is consistent with a projectile interception model using recent target movement and a prediction horizon.
interpretations.basis: Targeting follows moving opponents in projectile/spear combat; many different algorithms can produce the same visible motion.

interpretations.claim: The video uses the same aimbot as the earlier debug-object screenshot.
interpretations.basis: Only generic latency terminology overlaps; aimsteps, pingSteps and the implementation are not visible.

not_established: the precise latency formula or units of every custom field
whether full RTT or half RTT is used
the meaning of aimsteps and pingSteps
whether positions come from game state or image recognition
which outgoing game packets are used
